title: Underived (Pull)
statement:
For a morphism $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of commutative condensed rings
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]) and a morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$, the underived
*(Pull)* comparison is the natural isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X}\circ f^*\;\cong\;f^*\circ\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Y}\colon
\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\longrightarrow\Mod_{\Lambda'_X},
$$

with $f^*$ the pullback of module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]), defined as
the conjugate of the isomorphism of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso] along the adjunctions
$f^*\dashv f_*$ (over $\Lambda$ and over $\Lambda'$) and
$\operatorname{Ext}\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]), in the sense of
[def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso].

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: (CategoryTheory.conjugateIsoEquiv (A_Y.comp B_prime) (B.comp A_X)).symm e. Here A_X and A_Y are Ext_{a_X} ⊣ Res_{a_X} and Ext_{a_Y} ⊣ Res_{a_Y} from sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars, B is f^*_Λ ⊣ f_{*,Λ} and B_prime is f^*_{Λ'} ⊣ f_{*,Λ'} from sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, and e is def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso. Composition of adjunctions is CategoryTheory.Adjunction.comp at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Basic.lean:567. With Lean's diagrammatic functor composition, A_Y.comp B_prime has left adjoint Ext_{a_Y} ⋙ f^*_{Λ'} and right adjoint f_{*,Λ'} ⋙ Res_{a_Y}; B.comp A_X has left adjoint f^*_Λ ⋙ Ext_{a_X} and right adjoint Res_{a_X} ⋙ f_{*,Λ}. Thus e has exactly type R₁ ≅ R₂ and the inverse equivalence at Mates.lean:425-435 produces L₂ ≅ L₁, namely Ext_{a_X} ∘ f^*_Λ ≅ f^*_{Λ'} ∘ Ext_{a_Y}. This is the conjugate required by def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso, without identifying module objects with ordinary ModuleCat-valued sheaves. The general construction has no flatness, properness, finiteness or exactness hypothesis. All project-specific data remain the five statement dependencies; this match supplies the comparison from those data. Revalidated on the current DAG after the return: the module-functor dependency specifies f_* = Res_{eta_f} ∘ mapMod(f_*^Ab), f^* = Ext_{alpha_f} ∘ mapMod(f^*_Ab), and explicitly their lifted adjunction using the mate relation eta_f/alpha_f. These are the functors of B and B_prime above, for Lambda and Lambda_prime respectively; no replacement by restriction along an inverse of alpha_f, no use of composition comparisons, and no additional geometric hypothesis is involved.
